_notes: Universal card-extraction template. Every card (credit, debit, prepaid; any issuer) fills this same shape. Use null for 'not yet verified / unknown', use the string "N/A" for 'this field genuinely does not apply to this card' (e.g. cash_advance on a debit card, invite_only fields on an open-application card), and use [] for 'verified — this card has none of these'. Never delete a key because it doesn't apply — mark it N/A so downstream ingestion can tell 'not applicable' apart from 'not scraped yet'.

eligibility_engine.notes: Apply through the zagg.money app. A customer can apply for only one network variant (page FAQ). The UPI mobile number must match the card mobile number. AU says the criteria are only indicative.

category_surcharges.trigger_condition: From 1 Jul 2026: 1% on the whole month's fuel spend when one transaction exceeds ₹10,000 or the calendar-month total exceeds ₹25,000
1% on utility spend above ₹50,000 in a calendar month

components: If previous Total Amount Due was paid on time: 5% of principal outstanding + 100% of fees/charges + 100% of interest + due EMIs + 100% annual fee (if applicable) + 100% GST

open_questions: HELD (wave 3 re-check 2026-11-07): AU states rates as "X% Zagg Coins" and gives the value of a coin (₹0.25) but never says how many coins one percent means per ₹100 spent. Searched and read: the AU product page and FAQ (re-read), Cardmember Agreement 23.33, the AU press releases of 22 Sep 2025 and 9 Jul 2026, the KFS and MITC. None defines the unit. CMA 23.22 says only that Reward Points "as may be applicable on the credit card variant" are earned "for transaction amounts in multiples of ₹100", which does not map a percentage to coins. Leads for a person (NOT used as facts): Zaggle's own rewards policy (zagg.money/rewards-policy) says "3% of the transaction amount will be credited as Zagg Coins" for the YES Bank Zagg card, but it states it does not cover the AU card; and the 2,000-coin cycle cap fits a per-₹100 reading far better than a percent-of-value reading. Ask AU or Zaggle for the AU Zaggle rewards terms, or check a live statement, before writing rules. If 8% meant 8 coins per ₹100 the value is 2%; if it meant 8% of spend the value is 8%. No reward rule written so the importer does not guess; the structure is kept in notes below.
Network: both variants are issued and named by AU, so this is resolved as dual; the importer reads verified_network_research.
Whether the ₹99 + GST redemption fee in the KFS applies to Zagg Coin redemption through the zagg.money app: not stated for this program.
The CMA copy carrying the Zaggle clause is undated; the dated copy under /pdf/credit-card/ (16 May 2026) lacks it.

Page says Visa contactless earns 8% on transactions between ₹500 and ₹5,000 and 2% above ₹5,000; the CMA says 8% on contactless "not exceeding ₹5,000" with a ₹500 minimum for any earn. Consistent, noted for completeness.
notes: Structure as published (not modelled). RuPay variant: 4% Zagg Coins on zagg.money UPI up to ₹10,000 cumulative statement-cycle spend; 8% on the part above ₹10,000; 2% on UPI through other UPI apps; 2% on all other eligible retail. Visa variant: 8% on contactless of ₹500 to ₹5,000, 2% on contactless above ₹5,000; 4% on e-commerce; 2% on all other eligible retail. Page also lists 2% on POS and 2% on RuPay e-commerce.

Reward Points accrue only on eligible retail transactions of ₹500 or more. Capped at 2,000 Reward Points per statement cycle. Credited to the zagg.money account on statement generation. Valid 24 months from accrual (CMA 23.33; page FAQ says 2 years from the statement credit month).
Redemption only through the zagg.money app, minimum 1,000 points, as statement credit about 30 days after the request; once redeemed it cannot be reversed (CMA 23.33).
Forex 3.49%, cash limit 20%, fuel surcharge waiver 1% up to ₹100 per statement cycle on ₹400 to ₹5,000 (page, KFS). Contactless payments up to ₹5,000.
AU and Zaggle have a revenue sharing agreement as co-brand partners (page).
